items.title: Tom Malone interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, May 3, 2023

ctx.x: to be the same twelve notes. But you have to be able to play jazz, you have to play Latin, you have to play classical, you have to play whatever style of music, you just have to play it. There’s Hasidic pop recordings too, in Brooklyn. Mordechai Ben David, Avraham Fried, all those guys, Yeedle, all of them. They dress up like the Blues Brothers too.

Yes I noticed that. I just read, I thought it was pretty hip that, the way that thing came together and Dan Akroyd, your first assignment, if this is true, said, “Write an arrangement for some horn parts for Rocket 88.”

Well here’s the story: I was the arranger for Saturday Night Live from 1975 to 1985. And spring of 1978 the music director asked me to meet with John and Danny in John’s office at 2:00 on Monday afternoon. And it was just the three of us. And they were talking about, they were developing these characters, these guys that wore sunglasses day and night, and they were n’er do well blues musicians in Chicago.
